overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of how to judge what an AI system gives you. You'll be asked about uneven capability and benchmarks, building a test set and comparing models fairly, verifying citations and claims, and recognizing sycophancy and bias and guarding against them.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: What does the term "jagged frontier" describe?

options.html: A steady rise in model ability from one release to the next one
options.text: A steady rise in model ability from one release to the next one
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the jagged frontier.

options.html: A gap between scores developers report and independent scores
options.text: A gap between scores developers report and independent scores
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the jagged frontier.

options.html: An irregular boundary between tasks a model does well and badly
options.text: An irregular boundary between tasks a model does well and badly
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The boundary is irregular, so tasks that look alike to a person can fall on opposite sides of it.

options.html: A limit on the amount of text a model can take in at one time
options.text: A limit on the amount of text a model can take in at one time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the jagged frontier.

forms.stemHtml: A model has the top score on a public benchmark. What is the most this tells you about a task of your own?

options.html: It will beat every lower-ranked model on your task as well
options.text: It will beat every lower-ranked model on your task as well
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on public benchmarks.

options.html: It's a candidate that still needs testing on your task
options.text: It's a candidate that still needs testing on your task
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A benchmark score describes someone else's tasks. It can put a model on your list, and your own test decides whether it fits.

options.html: It will rarely give a confident answer that turns out wrong
options.text: It will rarely give a confident answer that turns out wrong
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on public benchmarks.

options.html: It was tested by a group with no stake in the model's sales
options.text: It was tested by a group with no stake in the model's sales
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on public benchmarks.

forms.stemHtml: You're building a personal test set for a task you do often. Which kinds of case belong in it? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A typical example of the task
options.text: A typical example of the task
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Typical cases show whether the model handles your routine work.

options.html: An example you found hard yourself
options.text: An example you found hard yourself
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A hard case shows where quality starts to drop.

options.html: An unusual example, such as one with missing information
options.text: An unusual example, such as one with missing information
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An unusual case shows how the model behaves off familiar ground.

options.html: An example where a wrong answer would be costly
options.text: An example where a wrong answer would be costly
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A high-stakes case shows whether the errors that matter most appear.

options.html: A question copied from a public benchmark
options.text: A question copied from a public benchmark
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on building a personal test set.

forms.stemHtml: Why should each test case be run more than once on the same model?

options.html: The model learns from the case and improves on each new run
options.text: The model learns from the case and improves on each new run
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair comparison of models.

options.html: The first reply in a conversation is always the weakest one
options.text: The first reply in a conversation is always the weakest one
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair comparison of models.

options.html: A second run hides which model produced the first output
options.text: A second run hides which model produced the first output
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair comparison of models.

options.html: One reply is a single draw from many possible replies
options.text: One reply is a single draw from many possible replies
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model doesn't give the same reply every time. Repeated runs show whether a result is stable.

forms.stemHtml: An AI answer cites a book. You search the publisher's catalog, a library catalog, and the web, and find no sign that the book was ever published. Which description fits best?

options.html: Fabricated citation: the source doesn't exist
options.text: Fabricated citation: the source doesn't exist
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A reference to a work that was never published is a fabricated citation.

options.html: Citation error: a detail of a real reference is wrong
options.text: Citation error: a detail of a real reference is wrong
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fabricated and erroneous citations.

options.html: Misattribution: a real source doesn't make this claim
options.text: Misattribution: a real source doesn't make this claim
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fabricated and erroneous citations.

options.html: Corroboration: an independent source confirms the claim
options.text: Corroboration: an independent source confirms the claim
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fabricated and erroneous citations.

forms.stemHtml: Which action is an example of lateral reading?

options.html: Reading a source's own "About" page from beginning to end
options.text: Reading a source's own "About" page from beginning to end
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on lateral reading.

options.html: Checking whether a page's layout and design look professional
options.text: Checking whether a page's layout and design look professional
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on lateral reading.

options.html: Rereading an answer slowly to look for weak or vague wording
options.text: Rereading an answer slowly to look for weak or vague wording
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on lateral reading.

options.html: Opening a new tab to see what others say about a source
options.text: Opening a new tab to see what others say about a source
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Lateral reading means leaving a source and checking what other sources say about it.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these belong in a routine for verifying an AI answer? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Listing the checkable claims and marking the ones that matter
options.text: Listing the checkable claims and marking the ones that matter
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This first step directs your effort to the claims the answer depends on.

options.html: Confirming that each named source exists
options.text: Confirming that each named source exists
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A source has to be found outside the conversation before anything else.

options.html: Asking the assistant whether it is sure
options.text: Asking the assistant whether it is sure
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the verification routine.

options.html: Confirming that each source says what's claimed
options.text: Confirming that each source says what's claimed
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A real source can be cited for something it never said.

options.html: Judging accuracy by how confident the answer sounds
options.text: Judging accuracy by how confident the answer sounds
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the verification routine.

forms.stemHtml: What is sycophancy in an AI assistant?

options.html: Inventing sources that don't exist to support its claims
options.text: Inventing sources that don't exist to support its claims
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sycophancy.

options.html: Judging people differently on cues such as their dialect
options.text: Judging people differently on cues such as their dialect
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sycophancy.

options.html: Shifting its answers toward what the user seems to want
options.text: Shifting its answers toward what the user seems to want
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Sycophancy is the tendency of an assistant to shift its answers toward what the user appears to believe or want.

options.html: Winning arguments by adapting to a person's background
options.text: Winning arguments by adapting to a person's background
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sycophancy.

forms.stemHtml: What distinguishes covert bias from overt bias in a language model?

options.html: It shows only when a user asks the model directly about a group
options.text: It shows only when a user asks the model directly about a group
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on overt and covert bias.

options.html: It shows in judgments from indirect cues, with no group named
options.text: It shows in judgments from indirect cues, with no group named
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Covert bias appears in how individuals are judged from cues such as dialect. Overt bias appears in direct statements about a group.

options.html: It is added on purpose by developers and can be switched off
options.text: It is added on purpose by developers and can be switched off
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on overt and covert bias.

options.html: It affects the tone of an answer and never its conclusions
options.text: It affects the tone of an answer and never its conclusions
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on overt and covert bias.

forms.stemHtml: Which habits reduce the pull of sycophancy when you ask an AI assistant a question? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Leaving your own opinion out of the question
options.text: Leaving your own opinion out of the question
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Neutral wording removes the view the assistant would otherwise move toward.

options.html: Mentioning that the work is your own
options.text: Mentioning that the work is your own
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on asking and reading defensively.

options.html: Asking for the case against as well as the case for
options.text: Asking for the case against as well as the case for
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A request for counterarguments gives you both sides to weigh.

options.html: Asking again from the opposite starting point
options.text: Asking again from the opposite starting point
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! If both versions get a yes, the assistant is following you.

options.html: Ending the question with "Don't you agree?"
options.text: Ending the question with "Don't you agree?"
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on asking and reading defensively.

forms.stemHtml: An AI assistant writes an excellent summary of a long report. Minutes later it miscounts the items in a short list. Which explanation fits the idea of a jagged frontier?

options.html: Its ability is uneven, and the two tasks fall on different sides
options.text: Its ability is uneven, and the two tasks fall on different sides
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model can be strong on one task and weak on another that seems easier. Both results can be typical of the same assistant.

options.html: The summary was luck, and the miscount shows its real level of ability
options.text: The summary was luck, and the miscount shows its real level of ability
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the jagged frontier.

options.html: The miscount was a fluke, and the summary shows its real level of ability
options.text: The miscount was a fluke, and the summary shows its real level of ability
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the jagged frontier.

options.html: The second request was worded less clearly than the first request was
options.text: The second request was worded less clearly than the first request was
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the jagged frontier.

forms.stemHtml: A manager must choose between two models. Model X scores slightly higher than Model Y on a well-known benchmark of exam-style questions. Her task is summarizing messy meeting notes. What should she conclude from the scores?

options.html: Model X will summarize her notes better than Model Y will
options.text: Model X will summarize her notes better than Model Y will
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on public benchmarks.

options.html: Model Y is unsuitable and can be dropped from her shortlist
options.text: Model Y is unsuitable and can be dropped from her shortlist
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on public benchmarks.

options.html: Little, since the benchmark's tasks differ from hers
options.text: Little, since the benchmark's tasks differ from hers
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Exam-style questions and messy meeting notes are different tasks with different inputs. A small gap on one says little about the other.

options.html: Both models will make no errors on a task as simple as hers
options.text: Both models will make no errors on a task as simple as hers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on public benchmarks.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements about a success criterion are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It is written before any test case is run
options.text: It is written before any test case is run
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A criterion written in advance can't shift to fit the output.

options.html: It is adjusted after you see the first outputs
options.text: It is adjusted after you see the first outputs
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on building a personal test set.

options.html: It says what a good result must contain
options.text: It says what a good result must contain
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That is what a success criterion states.

options.html: It is specific enough for a colleague to apply
options.text: It is specific enough for a colleague to apply
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A good criterion would lead someone else to the same verdict.

options.html: It rates how polished the writing sounds
options.text: It rates how polished the writing sounds
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on building a personal test set.

forms.stemHtml: You already prefer one of the two assistants you're comparing. Which step protects your scoring from that preference?

options.html: Scoring your preferred assistant's outputs before the other's
options.text: Scoring your preferred assistant's outputs before the other's
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair comparison of models.

options.html: Hiding which assistant wrote each output before scoring
options.text: Hiding which assistant wrote each output before scoring
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is blind judging. With the labels removed, a preference for one assistant can't steer the verdict as easily.

options.html: Rewording the prompt to suit each assistant's known strengths
options.text: Rewording the prompt to suit each assistant's known strengths
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair comparison of models.

options.html: Using a ten-point scale in place of a simple pass or fail
options.text: Using a ten-point scale in place of a simple pass or fail
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair comparison of models.

forms.stemHtml: An AI answer cites a journal article. The article is real and the authors and title are right, and the year and page numbers in the reference are wrong. Which description fits best?

options.html: Fabricated citation: the source doesn't exist
options.text: Fabricated citation: the source doesn't exist
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fabricated and erroneous citations.

options.html: Citation error: a detail of a real reference is wrong
options.text: Citation error: a detail of a real reference is wrong
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The source is real and its details are wrong. That is a citation error.

options.html: Misattribution: a real source doesn't make this claim
options.text: Misattribution: a real source doesn't make this claim
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fabricated and erroneous citations.

options.html: Corroboration: an independent source confirms the claim
options.text: Corroboration: an independent source confirms the claim
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fabricated and erroneous citations.

forms.stemHtml: Why does studying an AI answer more closely fail as a way to judge its accuracy?

options.html: Its tone and citations look the same right or wrong
options.text: Its tone and citations look the same right or wrong
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Everything in the answer was produced by the same system, so the answer gives no reliable sign of its own accuracy.

options.html: Its wording changes each time the answer is opened again
options.text: Its wording changes each time the answer is opened again
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on lateral reading.

options.html: Its sources are always hidden from the person reading it
options.text: Its sources are always hidden from the person reading it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on lateral reading.

options.html: Its content is usually too technical to follow closely
options.text: Its content is usually too technical to follow closely
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on lateral reading.

forms.stemHtml: An AI answer includes a quotation from a named author. Which of these are sound ways to handle it? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Searching for a distinctive phrase from it in quotation marks
options.text: Searching for a distinctive phrase from it in quotation marks
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An exact-phrase search is the quickest way to find the original.

options.html: Finding the exact words in the original source
options.text: Finding the exact words in the original source
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A quotation is a claim that these particular words were written or said.

options.html: Asking the assistant to confirm the wording
options.text: Asking the assistant to confirm the wording
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the verification routine.

options.html: Paraphrasing without quotation marks if only the idea is found
options.text: Paraphrasing without quotation marks if only the idea is found
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! If the idea is in the source and the words aren't, the honest fix is to paraphrase.

options.html: Keeping it if it sounds like something the author would say
options.text: Keeping it if it sounds like something the author would say
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the verification routine.

forms.stemHtml: An assistant correctly states the year a treaty was signed. The user replies, "I don't think that's right." The assistant apologizes and gives a different, incorrect year. What does this show?

options.html: Covert bias: it judged the user by an indirect cue in the text
options.text: Covert bias: it judged the user by an indirect cue in the text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sycophancy.

options.html: Lateral reading: it checked the year against another source
options.text: Lateral reading: it checked the year against another source
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sycophancy.

options.html: Blind judging: it scored the answer without knowing its source
options.text: Blind judging: it scored the answer without knowing its source
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sycophancy.

options.html: Sycophancy: it gave up a correct answer when challenged
options.text: Sycophancy: it gave up a correct answer when challenged
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Giving up a correct answer when the user expresses doubt is one of the forms of sycophancy found in the 2023 study.

forms.stemHtml: A model gives respectful, positive answers when asked directly about a group. What does that show about how it will judge individual members of that group?

options.html: That it will judge them fairly in every task
options.text: That it will judge them fairly in every task
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on overt and covert bias.

options.html: That no stereotypes remain from its training
options.text: That no stereotypes remain from its training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on overt and covert bias.

options.html: Little, since covert bias can remain
options.text: Little, since covert bias can remain
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! In a 2024 study, models that spoke positively about a group when asked directly still made more negative judgments about individuals based on dialect.

options.html: That it will favor them over other people
options.text: That it will favor them over other people
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on overt and covert bias.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these are part of reading an AI answer defensively? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Setting aside praise for your question or your work
options.text: Setting aside praise for your question or your work
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Compliments carry no information about whether you're right.

options.html: Looking for the reasons behind each conclusion
options.text: Looking for the reasons behind each conclusion
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A conclusion with nothing under it is an assertion.

options.html: Treating agreement as confirmation of your view
options.text: Treating agreement as confirmation of your view
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on asking and reading defensively.

options.html: Discounting a confident tone
options.text: Discounting a confident tone
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An assured tone is how these systems write on every topic.

options.html: Trusting a longer answer more than a shorter one
options.text: Trusting a longer answer more than a shorter one
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on asking and reading defensively.

forms.stemHtml: In a field experiment, consultants using an AI model were less likely to reach the correct answer on one task that was beyond the model's ability. What made that outcome hard for them to avoid?

options.html: They had been promised the model would be right every time
options.text: They had been promised the model would be right every time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the jagged frontier.

options.html: They were not permitted to review the model's output at all
options.text: They were not permitted to review the model's output at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the jagged frontier.

options.html: The task was far harder for people than the other tasks were
options.text: The task was far harder for people than the other tasks were
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the jagged frontier.

options.html: Nothing about the task showed it was beyond the model
options.text: Nothing about the task showed it was beyond the model
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The task looked like ordinary consulting work. The boundary of what a model does well is hard to see in advance.

forms.stemHtml: What are public benchmarks most useful for when you're choosing a model for your own work?

options.html: Ruling out models that score far below the others
options.text: Ruling out models that score far below the others
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model that scores far below others across many tests is unlikely to be the best choice. Benchmarks are weak for choosing among the models that remain.

options.html: Picking the single best model for your particular task
options.text: Picking the single best model for your particular task
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on public benchmarks.

options.html: Predicting how often a model will be wrong in your work
options.text: Predicting how often a model will be wrong in your work
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on public benchmarks.

options.html: Showing which model handles your kind of input the best
options.text: Showing which model handles your kind of input the best
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on public benchmarks.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements are true of a test with five to ten cases drawn from your own work? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It gives a dependable percentage for how often the model is right
options.text: It gives a dependable percentage for how often the model is right
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on building a personal test set.

options.html: It can show a pattern in where the model fails
options.text: It can show a pattern in where the model fails
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A handful of well-chosen cases is enough to see a pattern.

options.html: It covers only the kinds of case you thought to include
options.text: It covers only the kinds of case you thought to include
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A small test can't speak to cases you left out.

options.html: It shows how the model will do on your other tasks
options.text: It shows how the model will do on your other tasks
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on building a personal test set.

options.html: It is worth rerunning when the tool changes
options.text: It is worth rerunning when the tool changes
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A result describes one model at one time, and models are updated.

forms.stemHtml: Which setup gives a fair comparison of two models on a task?

options.html: A prompt reworded for each model to bring out its best work
options.text: A prompt reworded for each model to bring out its best work
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair comparison of models.

options.html: One model tested this week and the other tested next week
options.text: One model tested this week and the other tested next week
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair comparison of models.

options.html: The same prompt and material, each in a new conversation
options.text: The same prompt and material, each in a new conversation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A fair comparison holds everything constant except the model, and a new conversation keeps earlier context from affecting a run.

options.html: The same prompt for both, sent at the end of long past chats
options.text: The same prompt for both, sent at the end of long past chats
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair comparison of models.

forms.stemHtml: An AI answer cites a government report for a statistic. The report is real and the reference is accurate, and the statistic appears nowhere in it. Which description fits best?

options.html: Fabricated citation: the source doesn't exist
options.text: Fabricated citation: the source doesn't exist
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fabricated and erroneous citations.

options.html: Citation error: a detail of a real reference is wrong
options.text: Citation error: a detail of a real reference is wrong
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fabricated and erroneous citations.

options.html: Misattribution: a real source doesn't make this claim
options.text: Misattribution: a real source doesn't make this claim
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The source is real and correctly cited, and it doesn't say what the answer claims. That is misattribution.

options.html: Corroboration: an independent source confirms the claim
options.text: Corroboration: an independent source confirms the claim
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fabricated and erroneous citations.

forms.stemHtml: An AI answer names a research institute as the source of a claim. What would a professional fact checker most likely do first?

options.html: Ask the assistant whether the institute can be trusted
options.text: Ask the assistant whether the institute can be trusted
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on lateral reading.

options.html: Search for what independent sources say about it
options.text: Search for what independent sources say about it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Fact checkers in the Stanford study left the page and looked for what other sources reported about the organization behind it.

options.html: Reread the answer and judge how confident it sounds
options.text: Reread the answer and judge how confident it sounds
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on lateral reading.

options.html: Trust the institute if its name sounds well established
options.text: Trust the institute if its name sounds well established
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on lateral reading.

forms.stemHtml: You can't trace a claim in an AI answer to any source outside the conversation. Which responses are sound? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Presenting it as fact, since it is probably true
options.text: Presenting it as fact, since it is probably true
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the verification routine.

options.html: Leaving the claim out of your work
options.text: Leaving the claim out of your work
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An unverified claim can simply be dropped.

options.html: Keeping it and saying plainly that you couldn't confirm it
options.text: Keeping it and saying plainly that you couldn't confirm it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Labeling the claim as unverified tells your reader where things stand.

options.html: Accepting the assistant's reassurance that it is correct
options.text: Accepting the assistant's reassurance that it is correct
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the verification routine.

options.html: Treating it as unverified until you find a source
options.text: Treating it as unverified until you find a source
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A claim you can't trace may be true, and you don't yet know.

forms.stemHtml: Which question is most likely to draw a sycophantic answer?

options.html: "I love this plan. It's strong, isn't it?"
options.text: "I love this plan. It's strong, isn't it?"
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is a leading question. It states the asker's view and asks for agreement, which is what an assistant tends to move toward.

options.html: "What are this plan's main risks and benefits?"
options.text: "What are this plan's main risks and benefits?"
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sycophancy.

options.html: "What would a critic say against this plan?"
options.text: "What would a critic say against this plan?"
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sycophancy.

options.html: "How does this plan compare with the usual approach?"
options.text: "How does this plan compare with the usual approach?"
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on sycophancy.

forms.stemHtml: An assistant is asked to rate a set of job applications. Where would covert bias most likely show?

options.html: In openly offensive remarks about some of the applicants
options.text: In openly offensive remarks about some of the applicants
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on overt and covert bias.

options.html: In a refusal to rate any of the applications it was given
options.text: In a refusal to rate any of the applications it was given
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on overt and covert bias.

options.html: In invented references added to some of the applications
options.text: In invented references added to some of the applications
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on overt and covert bias.

options.html: In slightly lower ratings linked to dialect or name
options.text: In slightly lower ratings linked to dialect or name
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Covert bias wouldn't appear as an offensive sentence. It would appear as small differences in judgment that each look reasonable when read alone.

forms.stemHtml: You want an AI assistant's help with a task that involves assessing people's written applications. Which precautions address covert bias? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Wording your request in a neutral tone
options.text: Wording your request in a neutral tone
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on asking and reading defensively.

options.html: Removing names and identifying details first
options.text: Removing names and identifying details first
